title: Why commodity prices swing

predict.q: A crop market starts at Price 100, Quantity 100. A world recession shifts demand left by 10 at every price. Supply and demand are both **price inelastic**. What happens to price?

options.s: Price falls by about 5%, the same as the fall in quantity.
options.fb: A 5% price fall happens only with the elastic curves. Switch to "elastic" to see it.

options.s: Price falls by about 25%: much more than quantity falls.
options.fb: Right: with both curves inelastic, quantity can hardly change, so the price does the adjusting: 100 → 75 while quantity goes 100 → 95.

options.s: Price does not change, because supply is fixed in the short run.
options.fb: Supply is inelastic, not fixed. Even fixed supply would see the price fall when demand falls.

task: Move the demand slider to −10, then switch between "inelastic" and "elastic" curves.

target.do: Move the demand slider to −10 with the "inelastic" curves, then press Check.

takeaway: When supply and demand are both **price inelastic**, small shifts cause **large price swings**.
explore: Switch to "elastic": the same shift of −10 now moves the price only from 100 to 95.
